prompt: Hypothetical. Which statement about chasing a big move is correct?

options.text: Chasing a strong move is disciplined momentum, even when the planned price is gone
Buying after a big move, when the planned price is gone, is a sign of FOMO
FOMO only happens to beginners
A strong move means the planned price no longer matters

explanations.a: Chasing a move after the planned price is gone is FOMO. It is not discipline, because the trade is no longer the planned one.
explanations.c: Experienced traders can feel FOMO too. It is a human pull, not a sign of inexperience.
explanations.d: The planned price still matters. A strong move creates a new trade, which needs its own checks.

prompt: Hypothetical. You buy 17 shares at Rs 448 each. How much cash does the trade use, in rupees?
Hypothetical. The planned entry was Rs 400 with a stop at Rs 390. A late entry is at Rs 448 with a stop at Rs 420. The risk budget is Rs 500 in both cases. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The same Rs 500 of risk always buys 50 shares
The wider stop gives 17 shares, so the late trade is the same plan
The wider stop gives 17 shares, but the late trade is not the planned trade
The late trade is safer, because it uses less cash

explanations.a: The shares depend on the risk per share. A wider stop means fewer shares for the same rupee risk.
explanations.b: The share count changes, but the entry, the stop and the reason for the trade are all different. It is a new trade.
explanations.d: Less cash does not make the trade safer. The late entry still needs its own checks.

prompt: Hypothetical. You have won four trades in a row. You plan to double your size, because the method seems to work now. Which response fits the chapter?

options.text: Double the size, because four wins show skill
Keep the planned size and log the run, because four wins are a short sample
Trade more often so the streak lasts longer
Skip the journal, because the results are good

explanations.a: Four wins are a small sample. Doubling size on that basis is overconfidence.
explanations.c: More trades do not make a win streak more likely to last. Trading more often is an overtrading habit.
explanations.d: The journal is most useful when results look good. It shows whether the plan was followed.

prompt: Hypothetical. You read only the news that supports your trade idea and ignore the rest. What is this?

options.text: Research, because I am gathering information
Confirmation bias, because I look only for evidence that agrees with the idea
A good way to check the plan
Harmless, if I also read the chart

explanations.a: Research includes evidence that disagrees. Reading only one side is not research.
explanations.c: A plan check looks for reasons the idea could fail. Reading only supportive news does the opposite.
explanations.d: Reading the chart does not remove the bias from reading only one side of the news.

prompt: Hypothetical journal note: "Entered at market, will fix stop later." Which part of this note is the mistake?

options.text: Entering at the market price is always wrong
The stop is left for later, so the risk is not set before the trade starts
Writing a journal note at all
Nothing is wrong, because fixing a stop later is normal

explanations.a: The entry type alone is not the error here. The error is that the risk is not set before the trade.
explanations.c: Writing the note is the right habit. The mistake is what the note records.
explanations.d: A stop set after the trade is not a planned stop. The risk is open until it is set.
